purpose: Define SAFOR as a JSON-governed product executed by a compatible ordinary LLM chat using the host tools that actually exist, without requiring customer-installed SAFOR runtime software.
invariants: A compatible ordinary LLM chat is the primary SAFOR execution surface.
No domain path may require a customer-installed SAFOR runtime.
Optional reference code may validate or strengthen enforcement but never replaces the declarative chat contract.
Missing optional reference execution is not itself a product blocker.
Actual Git/provider capabilities and permissions are discovered and verified before effects are claimed.
